Subject: Production 5xx/429 spike impacting payments

Marissa —

We just experienced a large spike of 5xx errors and client 429s starting ~14:58 UTC that is causing payment processing failures in prod. Throughput dropped by ~60% and the retry storm from our side amplified traffic, which in turn caused multiple request timeouts and duplicate charge attempts on some flows.

What we have so far:
- 14:58 — 15:05 UTC: sudden increase in 5xx responses from Redwood endpoints (logs attached).
- 15:00 — 15:20 UTC: client-side 429s observed, followed by queued retries hitting our backend.
- Payment window at 17:00 UTC — if this is not stabilized we will miss the payroll batch.

We are attaching a compressed log snapshot (finsolve_5xx_log_snapshot_0503.zip). Please escalate immediately — this is Sev1 for us. We need a short bridge and executive visibility.

Requested immediate actions:
1) Immediate confirmation that Redwood is investigating host side/networking cause (latency/timeouts/egress behavior).
2) Quick mitigation steps we can take from our side (routing, retry throttling).
3) Exec-to-exec contact so we can coordinate escalation and consider contingency (manual payments).

Thanks —

Aisha / Marissa — joining the bridge now. Initial triage notes below (15:35 UTC):

Observations:
- We see a sharp uptick in request latency to the Dedicated VPC endpoints that serve FinSolve (p50 -> p95 increased from 60ms to ~1200ms).
- TCP retransmits and SYN retry rates on the customer peering path increased at ~14:56 UTC.
- Redwoods's egress layer returned an elevated number of 5xx errors initially, and our rate limiter observed a burst of concurrent inflight requests which generated 429 responses as a protective measure while backends recovered.
- Packet captures indicate intermittent connection resets consistent with connection-tracking exhaustion on a NAT device on the peering path.

Likely cause (working hypothesis):
- FinSolve's egress/NAT (or an intermediate F/W) is dropping or dropping/limiting ephemeral ports during the retry storm; asymmetric routing / BGP route flaps on the peered path magnify the effect. That leads to half-open TCP connections and ultimately timeouts that cascade into 5xx and client-side 429 behavior.

Immediate actions taken (15:36 — 15:45 UTC):
- Temporarily increased our request timeout and backoff thresholds on the affected route to reduce aggressive retry amplification.
- Whitelisted a fallback egress path for ~10% of traffic to reduce pressure on the problematic route.
- Captured VPC-level flow logs and packet traces; attached a visual diag (redwood_vpc_diag_0503.png).

Recommended next steps (for FinSolve):
1) Check NAT conntrack table sizes on your NAT/GW and increase ephemeral port range if possible.
2) Temporarily enable source-based affinity (stickiness) to avoid asymmetric paths while peering stabilizes.
3) If you have a spare VPN/egress path, route a portion of production traffic there for redundancy.

We'll keep the bridge open and I'll post continuous updates. If you can run an on-prem NAT conntrack dump and share, that will help confirm the hypothesis.

— Laura
